body:
## Problem

`.adlc/current-ticket.json` is the trust root every harness reads to decide which ticket is in flight. Its schema is documented nowhere, and ten hand-copied resolvers read it with two different key sets and three different hash-strictness levels:

| resolver | id keys accepted | ticketHash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| packages/tickets/lib/provenance.mjs (canonical) | id, ticket | required |
| packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs:545 (rails) | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs:1156 (build-gate) | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-cursor/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-antigravity/rails-checker.mjs | id, ticket | never checked |
| plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs:313 | id, ticket, ticketId | checked if present |
| plugins/adlc-pi/lib/rails-checker.mjs:64 | id, ticket, ticketId | never checked |

TEN resolvers (the tenth, plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/adlc-lifecycle.mjs, is advisory narration and was only found at P4 by the boundary test below), three strictness levels, two key sets. SEVEN do not accept `ticketId`.

Live consequence in THIS repo: the pointer is `{"ticketId":"T46","ticketHash":"fc7afc5a..."}`. Seven of the object-pointer resolvers -- including the canonical one -- resolve `id: null` => "no active ticket" => build-gate and the Claude Code rail hook FAIL OPEN and enforce nothing, while codex and pi enforce T46. Verified: `node -e "import('./packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.resolveActiveTicketId({dir:'.',env:{}})))"` prints `{id:null,conflict:false}`.

An object pointer whose id key is unrecognized (misspelled, or a legacy alias a given reader does not know) is silently read as "no pointer at all" => allow. That is a fail-open hole in a trust root. An UNPARSEABLE pointer correctly denies; an UNRECOGNIZED-SCHEMA pointer allows. No code writes the `ticketId` key -- it is hand-authored drift copied from the manifest's evidence field name, which is exactly what an undocumented schema produces.

Contributing causes:
- No documented pointer schema and no JSON schema file.
- The spec-14 generator (scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs) already exists and generates the ticket LOADER into three harnesses, but the RESOLVER was hand-ported into ten copies carrying "KEEP IN SYNC" comments instead.
- doctorTicketStore (packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs:22) reports `{name:'current-ticket', ok:true, present}` unconditionally -- it never parses, resolves, or hash-checks. This repo's stale pointer (T46 is merged work) passes doctor clean. Spec AC11 claims "current-ticket ... checks".
- The only programmatic writer (plugins/adlc-pi/lib/commands.mjs:226) does a bare non-atomic writeFileSync; every hook re-reads the file per tool call, so a torn read is reachable.
- ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT says only "conflicts with current-ticket.json" and never names the actual model: the active ticket is per-worktree state, and parallel work needs a separate worktree (spec 2 and 10.1).

## Build

1. **One canonical resolver.** Move the pointer contract into a new `packages/tickets/lib/pointer.mjs` (parse, validate, resolve, atomic write); `provenance.mjs` delegates to it. Port it into `scripts/ticket-readers/read-only-loader.mjs` and extend `scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs`'s output list to every harness that hand-copies a resolver (codex, claude-code, antigravity, opencode, cursor, pi). Delete the hand copies and their KEEP IN SYNC comments. `packages/build-gate/lib/active-ticket.mjs` re-exports the canonical resolution rather than reimplementing it.

2. **One key contract, fail-closed on drift.** Canonical `{"id": string, "ticketHash": string}` (spec 11). `ticket` and `ticketId` stay accepted DEPRECATED aliases in EVERY reader so no existing pointer bricks. An object pointer with no recognized id key is INVALID_CURRENT_TICKET => fail closed. This closes the fail-open hole. Deactivation is deleting the file, not writing `{}`. A bare string pointer stays a legacy form behind allowLegacyPointer.

3. **One hash strictness.** Every reader verifies `ticketHash` against `snapshot.ticketHashes[id]` and fails closed on mismatch (ACTIVE_TICKET_STALE). A missing hash is ACTIVE_TICKET_HASH_MISSING => fail closed under the strict default; only the documented 1.x bridge (allowLegacyPointer) downgrades it to a warning. No reader may silently skip a hash that is present.

4. **Doctor validates.** doctorTicketStore parses the pointer, resolves the id against the snapshot, verifies the hash, and reports ok:false plus the stable code for unparseable, unrecognized schema, absent ticket, missing hash, and stale hash; ok:true with a deprecation warning for an alias pointer. --json carries {present, id, code, deprecatedAlias}.

5. **Atomic writes.** Add `writeActiveTicket(root, ticket)` to pointer.mjs: write a temp file in the same directory then renameSync into place, always emitting `{id, ticketHash}`. plugins/adlc-pi/lib/commands.mjs uses it. A concurrent reader observes the old or the new pointer, never a partial one.

6. **Name the model in the error.** ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT states that the active ticket is per-worktree state and that parallel work on a second ticket needs its own worktree (`git worktree add`), not a second pointer.

7. **Document it.** Add packages/tickets/schemas/current-ticket.schema.json; document the schema, the worktree rule, and the alias deprecation in every docs/integrations/*.md that mentions the pointer, and record the deprecation in the 1.x-to-2.0 timeline in docs/specs/sharded-ticket-store.md.

8. **Repair this repo's live pointer** to the canonical form, or delete it since T46 is merged work (doctor will now report it).

## Decision record: hash strictness during 1.x (settled, do not re-litigate)

Repo evidence, gathered at P2:
- `packages/tickets/test/provenance.test.mjs:14` writes `{id, ticketHash}` -- the domain package is STRICT.
- `plugins/adlc-cursor/test/{rails-guard,pretool-dispatch}.test.mjs:28`, `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/review.test.mjs:47` all write `{id: currentTicket}` -- HASH-LESS. The harness layer's de facto contract omits the hash.
- Every `docs/integrations/*.md` offers the pointer as an option ("Active ticket via `ADLC_TICKET` or `.adlc/current-ticket.json`") and NEVER shows its schema, so a hand-written hash-less `{"id":"T1"}` is the expected state in the wild.

Therefore making harness readers strict-by-default would fail the existing harness suites AND deny every real install that took the documented file route -- punishing users for our own missing documentation. The decision:

- **The fail-OPEN hole is fixed unconditionally and immediately** (an object pointer with no recognized id key denies). This is the actual security defect and it is not bridged.
- **A missing `ticketHash` is bridged through 1.x**: harness readers default `allowLegacyPointer: true` and emit a deprecation warning; `@adlc/tickets`' own API keeps `allowLegacyPointer: false` (strict) as its default. A missing hash loses only stale-detection -- rails still enforce against the current ticket -- so it is a weaker guarantee, not a hole.
- **A PRESENT `ticketHash` is always verified in every reader**, bridge or not. Silently skipping a present hash is never permitted.
- **2.0 removes the bridge** (recorded in the spec-13 timeline by Build step 7).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 -- one implementation.** No hand-copied resolver remains; every harness resolver is the generated file or an import of it. A grep for 'KEEP IN SYNC' is NOT an acceptable verifier -- those comments were present and still wrong, and the grep false-positives on the pointer's legitimate appearances (a rail glob) and on ordinary \`ticket.id ?? '?'\` handling. The verifier is a boundary test that proves nobody parses the pointer themselves, and that fails on a planted hand-rolled reader. Verify: `node scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs --check` exits 0 AND `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs` exits 0 AND `node --test scripts/test/ticket-store-boundary.test.mjs` exits 0.
- **AC2 -- reader agreement, no fail-open.** A table-driven test runs every reader (canonical, generated, build-gate, and each harness) over a shared vector set and asserts identical decisions: `{"tickett":"T46"}` denies with INVALID_CURRENT_TICKET in all; `{"ticketId":"T46",...}` and `{"id":"T46",...}` resolve T46 in all. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='reader agreement'` exits 0.
- **AC3 -- live-bug regression.** The exact live pointer `{"ticketId":"T46","ticketHash":"fc7afc5a0a6517d908988afa6cd6eeb1a5fa918a8b91fd548f910798ef50191d"}` resolves to T46 in every reader, and no reader returns a no-active-ticket allow for an object pointer that carries any id-like key. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='live pointer regression'` exits 0.
- **AC4 -- hash strictness unified.** A PRESENT ticketHash that does not match the snapshot denies with ACTIVE_TICKET_STALE in every reader THAT HOLDS A SNAPSHOT. Boundary found at P4: @adlc/build-gate.resolveActiveTicketId({dir, env}) resolves IDENTITY and takes no snapshot (its bin loads the store separately), so staleness/absence/hash-missing are decidable only where the store is loaded; build-gate must still resolve the id and never report "no active ticket" for those vectors, which the rail asserts explicitly. A MISSING hash denies under the strict default (`@adlc/tickets`) and warns-but-resolves under the 1.x bridge default used by harness readers. Existing harness tests that write hash-less `{id}` pointers keep passing unchanged. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='hash'` exits 0.
- **AC5 -- doctor validates.** Doctor returns ok:false plus the stable code for unparseable, unrecognized-schema, absent-ticket, missing-hash, and stale-hash pointers; ok:true with deprecatedAlias:true for an alias pointer; ok:true for a canonical one. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='current-ticket'` exits 0.
- **AC6 -- atomic write.** writeActiveTicket renames into place from a same-directory temp file, and a test asserting no partial pointer is observable passes. Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='atomic'` exits 0.
- **AC7 -- error names the model.** The ACTIVE_TICKET_CONFLICT message contains "worktree". Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/pointer.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='conflict message'` exits 0.
- **AC8 -- no harness regression.** Verify: `node scripts/ticket-readers/generate.mjs --check && node scripts/codex-install-smoke.mjs . && node scripts/cursor-install-smoke.mjs . && node scripts/antigravity-install-smoke.mjs .` exits 0.
- **AC9 -- suite green.** Verify: `npm test` exits 0.
- **AC10 -- documented.** packages/tickets/schemas/current-ticket.schema.json exists and admits the canonical and alias forms while rejecting an unrecognized-key object; every docs/integrations/*.md that mentions the pointer shows the schema and the worktree rule. Verify: `node --test scripts/test/ticket-store-docs.test.mjs` exits 0.
title: Make .adlc/current-ticket.json one validated, fail-closed, generated contract across every resolver
